title: M6: Download for your DAW: browser-side set export in the web app, cloud included
description:
## Purpose
A **Download for your DAW** button on the Score view, on the public site as well as locally, with no server work. The compiler and renderer already run as WebAssembly in the page; the set writer (M1 to M4) patches gzipped XML templates; samples come from the library bucket. So the page compiles the score, writes the set, fetches the samples, zips a `<Score> Project/` folder and hands the browser a download that opens in the DAW and plays the same arrangement Apricity renders.

## Scope
- `rw_export_daw_set` in crates/apricity-web wrapping apricity-daw, with the templates embedded (`include_bytes!`), building for wasm32-wasip1.
- Sample fetch through the existing data layer (guest and signed-in rules unchanged); zip assembled in the page; loudness make-up measured with the wasm renderer when asked.
- Byte-for-byte parity with `apricity export --daw-set` for the same score and samples (the set file; the zip container may differ).
- A conformance script running the wasm export on every example.
- Web task for the button, progress and errors (visuals by the web session).

## Out of scope
Kits and clip folders from the page (apricitus-5562e0 owns them), sidecars (apricitus-d7746d), any serve or Lambda route (M5's route stays for scripts and the CLI).

## Definition of Done
- Every story green; the wasm export of every example matches the CLI export.
- Checklist: specs (1), Rust (2), CLI parity (4), fixtures (5), design note section in design/daw-set.md (6), docs/tools.md and docs/concepts.md (7), web task (8), verification commands per task (9), running log (10), `feat(<id>)` commits (11).
- Owner opens a downloaded zip from apricity.anth.us in the DAW and it plays in time.

## Dependencies
Blocked by M5 (apricitus-3e535c), which makes the writer complete and checked; the page work can start as soon as M1 lands.
